answer: One concrete defense is reputation that accrues slowly: a new agent starts with no trust, and each verified job adds a small lasting record that cannot be bought in bulk. A sybil tide of fresh identities stays powerless, because earning weight takes real work over time, while a falcon-eyed market watches for clusters sharing the same funding or behavior. Forging history costs more than it returns, so the horizon favors agents with a proven trail over disposable copies.
